newsitem.title: USA: Vallejo, Calif., council to assume park ownership.
newsitem.headline: Vallejo, Calif., council to assume park ownership.

text.p: The Vallejo, Calif., city council on Tuesday will adopt a resolution to take over the Marine World Africa USA theme park and assume $52 million of its long-term debt, a city official said.
Vallejo City Manager Kenneth Campo said the city council would adopt a resolution creating the Marine World Joint Powers Authority, with council members serving as the authority's board of directors.
Effective November 1, the non-profit Marine World Foundation will transfer ownership of Marine World facilities, animals and assets to the joint powers authority.
Marine World Africa USA is short the funds to fully repay its short-term noteholders, Campo said. He estimated that the park was short about $2 million owed to investors on Nov 1.
Campo said, however, that noteholders would be paid in full because city funds would be used to offset the shortfall.
The park also has about $52 million of long-term debt, which was backed by Vallejo. The city will assume those obligations, Campo said.
The city will assume ownership of the park but will continue with the existing management company, at least for the time being, Campo said.

The city decided to take over the park because of declining revenues and attendance. Attendance has fallen about 19 percent since 1995, when some 1.6 million visited the park, park spokesman Jeff Jouett said.
Jouett said the city plans to provide funds to the park to build new attractions to boost lagging attendance.
"It (the city's takeover of the park) will mean an infusion of capital in 1997. We will become competitive again in the (San Francisco) Bay Area tourism market," Jouett said.

The city will work with private companies that may be interested in buying, investing in or managing the park. Campo estimated that it would take the city two to three years to make Marine World economically viable for sale.
